text: Circadian rhythms regulate human epidermal stem cells: core clock genes peak in phased waves across 24 hours, each linked to transcript subsets temporally segregating responses to proliferation/differentiation cues (TGFβ, calcium). Arrhythmia impairs stem cell function in vitro and in vivo, possibly contributing to aging and carcinogenesis. Using FANTOM5, covering most human tissues and cell types, an atlas of active in vivo-transcribed enhancers was produced; enhancers resemble CpG-poor mRNA promoters, generating bidirectional, exosome-sensitive, short unspliced RNAs, enabling regulatory program comparison, identification of disease-associated regulatory SNPs, and classification of cell-type-specific versus ubiquitous enhancers. p38MAPK drives age-induced expression of multiple cell cycle inhibitors: dominant-negative p38(AF) mice (Thr180/Tyr182 mutated) show attenuated p38 signaling and inhibitor expression in organs including pancreatic islets, and aged p38(AF/+) mice display enhanced islet proliferation and regeneration versus wild-type littermates.
